chunks: And it was narrated from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī that he said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who forgot a word from the adhan and then remembered it when he had finished the adhan and the iqamah.
He said: “He returns to the word that he forgot and says it, then he should say from that word to its end, and he does not repeat the entire adhan nor the iqamah.”

key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the second call announcing the immediate start of salat
key_terms.حَرْفًا: a word or uttered part omitted from the formula
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: he goes back to the missed point

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets part of the adhan and remembers after finishing the iqamah, must he repeat everything?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who omits part of the adhan and only remembers after completing both the adhan and the iqamah. He should return to the omitted part and continue from there to the end, without repeating the whole adhan or the iqamah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.894 - It was narrated from Ammar al-Sabati that He said:
"Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about a man who forgot a word during the adhan (call to prayer) and remembered it after completing the adhan and iqamah (second call to prayer).
The Imam said: "He should go back to the word he forgot, say it, and then continue from that point to the end. He does not need to repeat the entire adhan or the iqamah."
